Our work proves that models at the frontier can be trained across independent, globally distributed compute, without a hyperscaler and without a permission layer.

Grail handles reinforcement learning post-training. Each layer works on its own and composes with the others, and all of them are built to be used by people who do not work for us.

Training frontier models today requires either enormous capital or a job at one of a handful of labs. That concentration decides which ideas get tested, which researchers get to contribute, and which countries are left out of the next generation of AI. We are building the alternative: open infrastructure where a researcher in Nairobi or Buenos Aires can contribute compute, train on commodity hardware, and build on openly trained models without asking anyone's permission.

The next decade of AI research belongs to labs that can train at scale without permission. Covenant is building the ground they will stand on.

entity.name: Cognitive AI Research & Application
entity.description:
CAIRA is a governed, evidence-anchored AI research engine built for organisations that need accuracy, traceability, and domain integrity. Earlier versions, CairAssist and Cairity proved that teams wanted more than structured prompting and clean document generation. They needed a system that could understand scientific complexity, maintain provenance, and produce outputs that meet clinical, policy, and publication-grade standards.

That evolution led to SuperNova, CAIRA’s federated small-language-model engine engineered specifically for healthcare, science, and regulatory work. SuperNova operates on the Maya governance layer, which enforces reasoning discipline, source verification, and auditability across every interaction. Instead of probabilistic answers, it delivers accountable intelligence - structured, explainable, and compliant.

One of CAIRA’s most significant advances is its Microsoft Azure-enabled inclusion interface, powered by the Maya Voice Integration layer. Users can now move fluidly between typing, speaking, and conversational reasoning without losing context or structure. A clinician can draft part of a summary in text, switch to voice to refine analysis, then return to written mode, all while CAIRA maintains the evidence chain, citations, and regulatory alignment. This multimodal and multilingual continuity makes the system accessible to busy researchers, multilingual teams, and people who benefit from more natural modes of interaction.

Today, CAIRA supports clinical research groups, med-tech strategy teams, public-health organisations, and policy units. It produces literature reviews, white papers, regulatory briefs, grant frameworks, and presentation-ready outputs with precision and verifiable sourcing.

CAIRA generates new innovation and works for bespoke needs. It is not a chatbot; it is a governed intelligence platform designed for environments where trust, accuracy, and accountability are non-negotiable.

candidates.rationale: CAIRA offers an enterprise generative-AI platform and language-model engine that organizations could evaluate alongside OpenAI for research and regulated knowledge work.
